title: Isolated locally finite type points become finite after an etale base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $s\in S$ and let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in X$ be pairwise distinct points satisfying $f(x_i)=s$. Let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and assume that $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and that each $x_i$ is an isolated point of $X_s$. Then there are an etale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S,s)$ (so $U$ is a scheme, $U\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $u\in U$ maps to $s$), integers $m_i\geq0$, and open subschemes $V_{i,j}\subseteq X\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] such that: each $V_{i,j}\to U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; it has a unique point $v_{i,j}$ over $u$ with $\kappa(u)\subseteq\kappa(v_{i,j})$ a finite purely inseparable extension [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]; $v_{i,j}$ maps to $x_i$; every point of $(X\times_SU)_u$ mapping to $x_i$ is one of $v_{i,1},\ldots,v_{i,m_i}$; and $v_{i,j}=v_{i',j'}$ implies $(i,j)=(i',j')$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM (label lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-multiple-points-var), statement and proof at lines 12018-12090; Stacks Project Tag [02LM].

proof.text: Residue fields. For each $i$ the morphism $f$ is locally of finite type and $x_i$ is isolated in $X_s$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-residue-finite] the extension $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x_i)$ is finite [def-weil-residue-field]. (Stacks phrases this as: $f$ is quasi-finite at $x_i$ (Morphisms 01TH), hence $\kappa(x_i)/\kappa(s)$ is finite (Morphisms 01TG).)

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 02LM, lines 12056-12059

proof.text: Choice of the etale neighbourhood $(U,u)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separable-split-purely-inseparable-residue-fields] to $k=\kappa(s)$ and $K_i=\kappa(x_i)$ (finite over $\kappa(s)$ by step 1): it gives a finite separable algebraic extension $L/\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] such that for every $i$ the ring $L\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x_i)$ has finitely many primes and each of its quotients by a prime is a field, finite purely inseparable over $L$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. (In Stacks: $L_i\subseteq\kappa(x_i)$ the separable closure of $\kappa(s)$, $L$ a finite Galois extension receiving every $L_i$.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-neighbourhood-prescribed-residue-field] to $s$ and $L$: there are an etale morphism $\varphi:U\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $u\in U$ with $\varphi(u)=s$ and a $\kappa(s)$-isomorphism $L\cong\kappa(u)$. Transporting along this isomorphism (which induces a ring isomorphism $L\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x_i)\cong\kappa(u)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x_i)$ compatible with the maps from $L$ and $\kappa(u)$), for every $i$ the ring $\kappa(u)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x_i)$ has finitely many primes, and the quotient by any prime $\mathfrak p$ is a field which is a finite purely inseparable extension of $\kappa(u)$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 02LM, lines 12060-12068 (choice of L_i, L, and (U,u) by Lemma 02LF, more-morphisms-lemma-realize-prescribed-residue-field-extension-etale, line 10138); the field theory is packaged in the new node

proof.text: The points $y_{i,j}$. Let $X_U=X\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p:X_U\to X$ and $q:X_U\to U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] the points $y\in X_U$ with $p(y)=x_i$ and $q(y)=u$ are in bijection with the primes of $\kappa(x_i)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(u)\cong\kappa(u)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x_i)$, a finite set by step 2; enumerate them as $y_{i,1},\dots,y_{i,m_i}$ ($m_i\ge0$). Points with different $i$ are different since their images under $p$ are, so all the $y_{i,j}$ are pairwise distinct, and they are exactly the points of $X_U$ over $u$ mapping to some $x_i$. For the prime $\mathfrak p_{i,j}$ attached to $y_{i,j}$ the quotient $(\kappa(x_i)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(u))/\mathfrak p_{i,j}$ is a field (step 2), so by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] it is isomorphic to $\kappa(y_{i,j})$ compatibly with the maps from $\kappa(u)$; hence $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(y_{i,j})$ (induced by $q$) is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 02LM, lines 12070-12079 (points of X_U over x_i and u via Schemes, Lemma 01JT, schemes-lemma-points-fibre-product, line 3265, including its residue field clause)

proof.text: Hypotheses for the elementary case. The second projection $q:X_U\to U$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. Each $y_{i,j}$ lies over $x_i$ and $u$, and $x_i$ is isolated in $X_s$; by [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-base-change] (with $g=\varphi:U\to S$) the point $y_{i,j}$ is isolated in the fibre $(X_U)_u$ of $q$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre].

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 02LM, lines 12079-12081 (Morphisms, Lemma 01TM, morphisms-lemma-base-change-quasi-finite, with 01TH)

proof.text: Application of the elementary case. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-finite-multiple-points-elementary] to $q:X_U\to U$, the point $u$ and the finitely many points $y_{i,j}$: there are an etale morphism $\psi:U'\to U$ and $u'\in U'$ with $\psi(u')=u$ and $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(u')$ an isomorphism, and open subschemes $V_{i,j}$ of $X_U\times_UU'$, each finite over $U'$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with exactly one point $v_{i,j}\in V_{i,j}$ over $u'$, which maps to $y_{i,j}$ with $\kappa(y_{i,j})\to\kappa(v_{i,j})$ an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] (lower square $X_U\to X$ over $U\to S$, upper square $X_U\times_UU'\to X_U$ over $U'\to U$), $X_U\times_UU'$ with the composite projection to $X$ and its projection to $U'$ is a fibre product $X\times_SU'$ of $f$ and $\varphi\circ\psi$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; so the $V_{i,j}$ are open subschemes of $X\times_SU'$, finite over $U'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2) the composite $\varphi\circ\psi:U'\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and it maps $u'$ to $s$: $(U',u')$ is an etale neighbourhood of $(S,s)$. This is the neighbourhood and these are the opens of the statement.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 02LM, lines 12083-12089 (application of Lemma 02LL, more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-multiple-points, line 11974); the identification X_U x_U U' = X x_S U' is implicit there

proof.text: Verification (omitted in Stacks; written by the agent). Property (i) and the uniqueness in (ii) hold by step 5. Residue fields: the square formed by $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(y_{i,j})$, $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(u')$, $\kappa(y_{i,j})\to\kappa(v_{i,j})$, $\kappa(u')\to\kappa(v_{i,j})$ commutes [def-weil-residue-field] and its two maps out of $\kappa(u)$, $\kappa(y_{i,j})$ to the primed fields are isomorphisms, so $\kappa(u')\to\kappa(v_{i,j})$ is isomorphic to $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(y_{i,j})$, finite purely inseparable by step 3 [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]; this is (ii). The point $v_{i,j}$ maps to $y_{i,j}$ and hence to $x_i$ in $X$; distinct pairs $(i,j)$ give distinct $y_{i,j}$ (step 3), hence distinct $v_{i,j}$; this is (iv) and the first half of (iii). Finally let $w$ be a point of $X\times_SU'=X_U\times_UU'$ over $u'$ mapping to $x_i$; it corresponds to a point of the fibre $(X\times_SU')_{u'}$ and conversely [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Its image $y$ in $X_U$ lies over $u$ and $x_i$, so $y=y_{i,j}$ for some $j$ (step 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] for $X_U\times_UU'$, the points over $(y_{i,j},u')$ correspond to the primes of $\kappa(y_{i,j})\otimes_{\kappa(u)}\kappa(u')\cong\kappa(y_{i,j})$ (as $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(u')$ is an isomorphism), a field with exactly one prime; since $v_{i,j}$ is such a point, $w=v_{i,j}$. So no other point of $(X\times_SU')_{u'}$ maps to $x_i$: this is the second half of (iii).

lean.statement: theorem exists_etale_local_finite_multiple_points {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (s : S) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s) (hdistinct : Function.Injective x) (hisolated : ∀ i, IsOpen ({f.asFiber (x i)} : Set (f.fiber (f (x i))))) : ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (φ : U ⟶ S) (u : U), Etale φ ∧ φ u = s ∧ ∃ (m : Fin n → ℕ) (V : (i : Fin n) → Fin (m i) → (pullback f φ).Opens) (v : (i : Fin n) → (j : Fin (m i)) → (V i j).toScheme), (∀ (i : Fin n) (j : Fin (m i)), IsFinite ((V i j).ι ≫ pullback.snd f φ) ∧ ∃ (hv : ((V i j).ι ≫ pullback.snd f φ) (v i j) = u), (∀ w : (V i j).toScheme, ((V i j).ι ≫ pullback.snd f φ) w = u → w = v i j) ∧ (letI := ((U.residueFieldCongr hv.symm).hom ≫ ((V i j).ι ≫ pullback.snd f φ).residueFieldMap (v i j)).hom.toAlgebra Module.Finite (U.residueField u) ((V i j).toScheme.residueField (v i j)) ∧ IsPurelyInseparable (U.residueField u) ((V i j).toScheme.residueField (v i j))) ∧ ((V i j).ι ≫ pullback.fst f φ) (v i j) = x i) ∧ Function.Injective (fun a : (i : Fin n) × Fin (m i) ↦ (V a.1 a.2).ι (v a.1 a.2)) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin n) (w : ↥(pullback f φ)), pullback.snd f φ w = u → pullback.fst f φ w = x i → ∃ j : Fin (m i), w = (V i j).ι (v i j))

statement_change.what: Repeated inputs are incompatible with simultaneous exhaustion and globally distinct output points: for f=id of Spec k, n=2 and x_1=x_2 the same sole lift must occur in both lists, contradicting (iv). Stacks 02LM implicitly treats the listed points as distinct: its global distinctness clause (iv), together with exhaustion (iii), requires this. The elementary lemma 02LL itself permits repetitions. Also the phrase no other point must mean no point outside the entire list for i, not outside an individual singleton; separable residue extensions may give m_i>1. Make both conventions explicit.
